lines: November the ninth. Day one of the war.
It began with an empty trench. Two armies, and not a single soldier on the line.
Then, on the evening of November the eighth, the first name went up. Valentin Hodnepijumal. The first soldier of the Hegemony.
Not long after, Felix Kagr answered for the Concord.
All through the night and the next day, they kept coming. Comment by comment, the trenches filled.
For most of the day the Hegemony stayed ahead. Then, close to midnight, the Concord caught up, and passed them.
By the first morning paper, one hundred and twenty soldiers held the line. Hegemony, fifty-seven. Concord, sixty-three.
The first shots came the same day.
A Concord sniper, Ulrich Gpt, hit Wendel Freddie of the Hegemony. The first man badly wounded in this war.
Two more were grazed. Nobody died. Not yet.
But that night, the front was not only about rifles.
Edmund Biwott of the Concord threw a tin of tobacco into the enemy trench. The note said: for the one who sings.
It was picked up by Valentin Hodnepijumal. The very first soldier of the Hegemony kept the tin.
Out in no man's land, Yann Vee and Silas Zdsh crawled into the same shell hole. They stared at each other.
Then each crawled home. Neither has told anyone.
And a race had begun. The first army to reach one hundred soldiers takes Verdel Ridge, and its guns.
Concord sixty-three. Hegemony fifty-seven. Thirty-seven more, and the heights are theirs.
Day one. One hundred and twenty soldiers. Three wounded. No dead.
This was Front News. Next time: the race for the ridge.
